postTitle: Moving Countries: Rebuilding Your Financial Identity
topic: A border resets your credit file, and rebuilding it follows an order

assumptions.notes: No euro figures. Illustrative newcomer with twenty years of on time repayments in one country, which appear as no file in the next, because credit files are held nationally. Rebuild order from the post: ID and a tax number, a basic bank account, proof of address, income on the record (three to six months of wages paid in), then small reported credit where the local system scores people that way, then a credit report check after six months. Systems vary by country. Not immigration advice.

Your credit history does not cross the border with you. Few people hear that before they move.
No bank account without an address. No address without a bank account. Many newcomers hit this loop.

caption.instagram:
Twenty years of paying every bill on time. Move countries, and a lender sees nothing at all.

Credit files are held country by country, so a lender in a new country usually cannot see one held abroad. Rebuilding has an order, because each step produces the document the next one asks for: an ID and a tax number, a basic bank account, proof of address, wages paid in for three to six months, then small reported credit where the local system scores people that way.

After six months, a common step is to request the new credit report and check it for errors, which are frequent with foreign names and spellings.
